newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek depos, forwards up, bonds stable.
newsitem.headline: Greek depos, forwards up, bonds stable.

text.p: Greek depos were firmer and forex forwards were trading higher in tenors up to six-months on funding for the upcoming auction of fixed coupon bonds and the central bank's depo tender on Wednesday, dealers said.
Bonds were steady with an upward bias on thin volume and ecu/drachma rose a bit on ecu buying from local players, trading around 309.70/75.
"Depos are up more than 10 basis points across-the-board," said a dealer at a private bank. "Forex forwards are also up with the rise more accentuated in tomnext funds."
The dealer attributed the pick up in rates to funding for the planned fixed coupon bond auction in mid-July and the central bank's fixed rate depo tender on Wednesday.
"Tomnext is up because some banks seek to borrow at rates well below 11.90 percent, the rate at which the central bank soaks 14-day funds in its Wednesday depo tender," the dealer said.
The finance ministry is going to auction fixed coupon bonds on July 15, if it sticks to its tentative borrowing schedule released in early June.
Secondary bond market volume continued to be thin and bond prices were stable with an upward bias, dealers said.
"The market is seeking direction and what we see is minor price moves, usually on the upside," said a senior bond dealer at a private bank.
The mark was quoted at 157.30/40 from Monday's 157.550 fix, the dollar at 276.07/17 drachmas from 274.680 and the ecu at 309.65/75 from 309.75 drachmas.

"Ecu/drachma opened at 309.60/65 and has firmed a bit to 309.70/75 on ecu buying from locals," said a senior forex dealer at a foreign bank. "Dollar/drachma is up on the heels of a firmer dollar/mark."
